title: Customer VPC handover & approval flow notes
content:
Status: rough playbook / brainstorming notes for handing over customer-managed VPCs and integrating approval gates + audit logging requirements. Not final.

Goal:
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction handover that ensures customers can bring their own networking while we meet audit, compliance, and ops SLAs.
- Define minimal approval gates so we can automate most steps but keep human oversight for risky changes.
- Specify audit log design (schema, retention tiers, sensitive-field handling) that works across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Scope (this doc):
- Customer VPC handover checklist (networking + routing + DNS + certs) for Private deployments.
- Approval flow for enabling new cross-connects, BGP peering, CIDR updates, and KMS/HSM key handovers.
- Audit log requirements: what to capture, where to ship, retention buckets, encryption, redaction.
- Observability + alerts for failed handovers or missing logs.

Out of scope (for now):
- Deep implementation of on-prem appliance install (separate doc).
- Billing contract/legal terms—work with Sales/Legal templates.

High-level handover steps (suggested):
1) Pre-handover runbook + kickoff meeting (SE + customer network engineer + SRE).
   - Share a pre-checklist: expected CIDRs, route table plan, NAT requirements, expected throughput, peering window.
   - Link to template: Confluence "Private Deployments Checklist".
2) Identity & keys
   - Confirm KMS integration plan: customer-managed KMS OR Redwood-managed with customer key escrow.
   - If customer KMS: collect key ARN + policy; if Redwood KMS: generate wrapped key and store in escrow vault.
   - Approvals: security-review required for customer KMS (ticket: JIRA-PD-782).
3) Network connectivity handoff
   - Peering/BGP: agree on ASN, prefixes, keepalive, timers, and maintenance window.
   - Firewall rules: customer to provide explicit ingress/egress lists. We require audit-proof change records for any firewall rule changes after handover.
   - Public endpoints: if customer wants static IPs, document allocation + expected lifetime.
4) Access & roles
   - Create RBAC roles for customer-admin, customer-network-operator, redwood-oncall.
   - Approval gate: any role that enables network changes must be multi-approver for first 3 months.
5) QA & smoke tests
   - Test generation request, sample inference calls, trace through observability to ensure flows are captured in logs.
6) Final signoff
   - Two approvers required (SE + SRE lead OR Security + SE) to mark the handover complete.

Proposed approval gates (automation-first, human fallback):
- Gate A: Initial network attachment request (customer fills template) -> automated validations (CIDR overlap, ASN conflict, DNS name checks). If validations pass, auto-approve. If any validation fails, create an SRE review ticket and require 1 human approver.
- Gate B: High-risk change (CIDR change, route withdraw, open 0.0.0.0/0 ingress) -> require 2 approvers (SRE + Security) and scheduled maintenance window.
- Gate C: KMS/Key escrow access or export -> require Security + legal signoff. Locked via short-lived signed tokens for the exchange.

Implementation notes for approval system:
- Use existing internal workflow engine (orchestration service) to record requests; attach artifact: JSON payload of requested networking change.
- Every gate evaluation produces an immutable approval record (approved_by list, approver_roles, timestamp, justification). Store record as an audit event (see audit design).
- Keep approval UI minimal: quick approve/deny + comment. Support Slack-based approvals for low-risk changes but log the Slack approval into the same audit stream.

Audit log spec (draft):
- Required fields for each audit event (canonical): event_id, event_type, actor_id, actor_role, timestamp_utc, resource_type, resource_id, action, request_payload_hash, outcome, approver_ids (if applicable), retention_bucket.
- Supporting telemetry: request latency, request_source_ip, region, trace_id, correlation_id.
- Sensitive fields: request_payload may contain PII/keys. We should avoid storing raw secrets. Approach: store a deterministic hash of payload + minimal normalized fields. If payload contains structured user data (email, username), we either redact or store hashed value with salt per-customer.
- Retention buckets (proposed):
   * short-term operational (30 days) - high fidelity (full structured events, indices) - used for debugging and realtime alerts.
   * compliance (1 year) - reduced fidelity (no raw secrets, aggregated indices) - used for incident review and customer audits.
   * archival (7 years) - minimal index (event_id, actor_id hash, timestamp, outcome) - legal/compliance only.
- Encryption: all audit streams must be encrypted at rest with customer or Redwood KMS; in transit use TLS. For customer-managed KMS, enforce envelope encryption (customer CMK wraps service key).
- Shipping options: Kafka topic per-customer (recommended), syslog forwarder, or direct S3 delivery. Provide standard connectors to Splunk/Datadog/ELA.

Operational observability & alerting:
- Missing logs: if a customer-configured sink stops receiving events for >5m -> auto page SRE and message customer.
- Unexpected volume spikes: alert if event rate deviates >3x baseline for >10m. Possible indication of runaway approval loop or abuse.
- Approval backlog metric: time-to-approve distribution; target median < 2h for auto-validated gates, <24h for human gates.

Network-specific audit items to capture:
- BGP session state changes (established, down, config update) with timestamp + reason.
- Route announcements/withdraws with prefix, next-hop, community tags.
- NAT translations creation/teardown (if managed by Redwood).
- Firewall rule CRUD with before/after snapshots (policy diffs).

Privacy & redaction patterns (proposal):
- Replace IPs with tokenized placeholders for archival bucket unless explicitly requested in an audit.
- Keys/credentials: never store raw; only store key_id and operation hash + who requested.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (pilot): pick 2 existing Private customers for pilot; run manual handover with richer human review, collect checklist feedback.
- Phase 1 (automation): implement Gate A auto-validation and the audit event schema; start shipping events to internal Kafka topic and to a compliance S3 bucket.
- Phase 2 (scale): enable Slack approvals + 2-approver flow for Gate B; enable customer-facing audit portal (read-only) for last 30 days.
- Phase 3 (hardening): implement retention lifecycle jobs, redaction tooling, and KMS-customer-key workflow.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we require customer-signed LOA for KMS key export/escrow? Legal input needed. (Assigned: Evelyn)
- How granular should the RBAC roles be? Start broad, then iterate. (Assigned: Miguel)
- Where do we surface approval metadata in Console? Minimal at first: request history per deployment + link to raw audit event. Product to propose UI mockups. (Assigned: Aisha)
- Is Kafka per-customer viable at scale? Ops to validate retention/cost. Otherwise S3-first. (SRE investigation item).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: storing raw customer network configs accidentally -> mitigation: default redact all payloads; require explicit opt-in to store raw JSON for debugging and record reason + approval.
- Risk: long approval turnaround blocks customer migrations -> mitigation: SLA targets + auto-approvals where safe; runbook for emergency expedited approvals.

Next steps (practical):
- Convert this note into a PRD skeleton: introduce sections for API spec + audit schema + console UX. (Owner: Aisha)
- SEs to run pilot kickoff with Customer X and Customer Y (target next month). (Owners: Miguel, Ravi)
- SRE to prototype Kafka topic and automated validator for CIDR conflicts (spike ticket: JIRA-PD-800). (Owner: Ravi)
- Security to review KMS escrow proposal and produce a short decision doc. (Owner: Evelyn)

Appendix: quick example audit event (human-readable):
- event_id: evt-20250210-0001
- event_type: network_attachment.request
- actor_id: user:alice@example.com -> store as hashed_actor in archival bucket
- timestamp: 2025-02-10T15:12:03Z
- resource_type: vpc-attachment
- action: create
- request_payload_summary: {cidr: 10.2.0.0/16, asn: 64512, peering: bgp} (payload stored as hash in compliance bucket)
- outcome: auto-approved
- approver_ids: []

Notes to self: keep this doc iterative. We should prioritize low-friction automation first and make the audit schema backwards-compatible. Reach out to Legal and Sales about required LOAs for key operations.

References:
- Confluence: Private Deployments Checklist (linked above)
- JIRA-PD-782 (KMS integration)
- JIRA-PD-800 (CIDR validation spike)
